claim: For a continuous-time birth–death population with \(N=3\), unit birth rates, and two environments whose death-to-birth ratios are \( (x,y)\) and \( (y,x)\) at mutant counts \(1,2\), let switching be composition-dependent: \( +\to- \) occurs at rate \(e\) at count \(1\) and \(M\) at count \(2\), with reverse rates \(M\) and \(e\). For \(0<x<y\) and \(e,M>0\), fixation from one mutant in environment \(+\) exceeds both fixed-environment probabilities if and only if \(xM^2+(xy-e)M-e(e+1)(y+1)>0\), equivalently \(M>M_*\) for the positive root \(M_*=[e-xy+\sqrt{(xy-e)^2+4xe(e+1)(y+1)}]/(2x)\). With only \(N=2\) individuals and one transient mutant-count state, switching cannot exceed the best fixed-environment fixation probability. For \(x=2,y=3,e=1/10,M=10\), the switching model gives \(181/1373\), above the fixed-environment values \(1/9\) and \(1/10\).

correctness.rationale: The fixed-environment probabilities follow from the birth–death increment recurrence. The \(N=2\) backward equations give nonpositive differences from the better frozen probability. For \(N=3\), the four-state backward system has a strictly diagonally dominant Z-matrix, so its determinant is positive; exact elimination gives the signed difference as \((y-x)F/((1+x+xy)\Delta)\). The example is checked by exact rational arithmetic. The claim is restricted to this model and initial state.

originality.rationale: The central distinction is population-conditioned switching, not environmental switching in general. The closest inspected 2014 theory explicitly assumes that the environmental chain evolves independently of the population state; the 2017 fluctuating-carrying-capacity model also uses exogenous switching. Neither supplies the exact state-conditioned threshold or the N=2/N=3 sharp cutoff. Search failure is not treated as proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The exact criterion identifies the smallest population size at which composition-dependent switching can beat both frozen environments in this model family, and it gives a necessary-and-sufficient threshold in the feedback rate. The worked example shows that the effect can occur even when both fixed environments have death-to-birth ratios above one at every transient count. This is a motivated structural boundary, not merely a numerical example or a general claim about all biological populations.
